case_study_insert.main_stem: Crossport Shuttle Logistics (CSL) is a partnership in the port shuttle trucking sector, running container shuttles between the container port, an inland rail yard and regional distribution depots. Founded in 2016 by Nadia Karim and Tom Whitmore, it employs a workforce of 64 and operates a flat structure with democratic leadership. CSL plans to invest $780,000 in 12 new electric port-shuttle trucks for its busiest container routes, financed by $480,000 hire purchase and $300,000 retained profit. It has fixed costs of $390,000 a year, a variable cost of $69 a unit and a selling price of $95, and currently produces 24,000 units a year. CSL faces one operational problem: labour turnover among shuttle drivers has reached 12%, undermining terminal turnaround times.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: Operations Log — Q3 2026: CSL's fleet completed 6,100 port runs in the quarter at an on-time rate of 93.5%, up from 88.0% a year earlier. Average turnaround at the container terminal fell to 41 minutes from 55 minutes. Empty running dropped from 22% to 14% of total miles. Market research of 320 freight forwarders found that 63% would pay more for zero-emission shuttle capacity and 57% require electric-delivery certificates for port contracts. A training needs analysis shows 9 of 64 drivers have not completed electric-truck familiarisation; courses at the haulage training centre cost $800 per driver. A training needs analysis found that drivers need on-the-job training in electric-truck handling and off-the-job training at the freight college before the new trucks enter service.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Crossport Shuttle Logistics for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Business Bulletin (November 2026): (1) Wholesale diesel prices have risen 16.4% year-on-year, raising fuel costs for diesel shuttle fleets. (2) The national minimum wage will rise by 6.3% from $13.20 to $14.03 per hour from April 2027, raising wage bills across road freight. (3) The central bank has raised the base interest rate from 4.75% to 5.5%, increasing the cost of new vehicle finance for logistics businesses.

questions.question_text: CSL plans to fund the 12 new electric port-shuttle trucks with $480,000 hire purchase. Explain two advantages for CSL of using hire purchase to fund the expansion rather than a bank loan.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Hire purchase matches the repayment profile to the trucks' earnings, with fixed monthly instalments that CSL can budget against a $69 variable cost and a $95 selling price. Unlike a bank loan, which typically requires a lump-sum principal and interest schedule and may demand blanket security over the partnership's assets, hire purchase keeps each truck self-funding from the $26 contribution each container move generates, so the $780,000 investment does not strain the $390,000 fixed-cost base.

Point 2: At the end of the hire purchase term the trucks become partnership property with no further capital outlay, whereas early-settled bank finance on new vehicles can leave asset and debt mismatched on the books. CSL also retains its $300,000 retained profit as a working-capital cushion against the 16.4% diesel-price rise, driver recruitment at 12% labour turnover, and the $800 per driver electric-truck courses, while the hire purchase provider carries the residual-value risk if electric battery technology improves faster than expected.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to Crossport Shuttle Logistics and its electric truck decision.

questions.question_text: CSL is launching its new electric port-shuttle service. Consider roadside billboards near the port and depots, radio advertising in the port city, or a targeted LinkedIn campaign to freight forwarders and shipping lines. Which should CSL choose to promote the launch? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Roadside billboards: Billboards near the port gate, rail yard and distribution depots would build brand recognition among drivers, port workers and passing commuters at low cost per impression. They suit simple visuals of the new electric trucks, but they cannot explain zero-emission certification, emissions reporting or contracted capacity, and the people who see them are overwhelmingly not the decision-makers at the 320 freight forwarders CSL researched — so awareness grows faster than contracts.

Radio advertising: Local radio would deliver a catchy launch message, reach thousands of commuters in the port city, and fit a tight tactical budget for a few weeks around the first 6,100 port runs of the electric fleet. However, the audience is fragmented across drivers, office workers and retirees rather than logistics buyers, complex messages are lost in short slots, and response is hard to attribute to specific contracts.

Targeted LinkedIn campaign: LinkedIn places CSL in front of the exact 320 freight forwarders and shipping-line procurement managers who sign port shuttle contracts, lets CSL showcase the 93.5% on-time rate, 41-minute turnaround and the zero-emission certificates demanded by 57% of forwarders, and generates measurable enquiries with cost per lead tracked post by post. It is slower and narrower than broadcast media and requires good content, but it targets switch-ready buyers directly.

Recommendation: CSL should choose the targeted LinkedIn campaign. The forwarders who specify port shuttle capacity respond to evidence — 63% would pay more for zero-emission shuttles and 57% need electric-delivery certificates — so direct, proof-led business marketing beats broad awareness advertising for a B2B launch. Billboards are rejected as awareness-only with no measurable contract conversion, and radio is rejected as audience-misaligned and unmeasurable; CSL should still use billboards cheaply for driver recruitment, where visibility does pay.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Limited knowledge or outline of the promotion options with minimal context.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in the context of CSL with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed discussion of all three options in the context of CSL with a well-justified recommendation explaining why billboards and radio advertising are rejected.

questions.question_text: CSL's labour turnover among shuttle drivers has reached 12%. Explain two benefits for CSL of using democratic leadership to improve motivation in its shuttle driver team.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Democratic leadership gives CSL's 64 drivers a genuine say in roster design, rest breaks and route sequencing, which raises job satisfaction and directly attacks the 12% labour turnover eroding terminal turnaround. Drivers consulted on depot handover routines feel respected as professionals, arrive committed to the shift, and are far less likely to resign chasing a competitor's schedule.

Point 2: Involving drivers surfaces practical intelligence from the port gate itself — for example which terminal lanes clash at peak, where empty running can be paired with backhaul loads, and how to hold the 41-minute turnaround. That frontline input cuts wasted miles (already down from 22% to 14%), lifts the 93.5% on-time rate further, and saves the $800 per replacement driver electric-truck familiarisation cost while protecting the 24,000 units a year that service CSL's hire purchase obligations. Drivers who shape the roster also push harder for backhaul loads, which can pull empty running below 14% and strengthen CSL's case for port zero-emission certification at renewal.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to CSL's driver turnover, on-time rate and turnaround.

questions.question_text: CSL must train 9 drivers on the new electric port-shuttle trucks. Consider on-the-job training on the port routes or off-the-job training at the haulage training centre. Which should CSL choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job training: Familiarisation drives on CSL's actual container routes teach the electric trucks' regenerative braking, battery management and charging discipline in real terminal conditions, cost nothing in fees, and keep the 9 drivers covering the 6,100 port runs while learning. Drawbacks are that supervisors lose productive hours, unsafe habits can pass from trainer to trainee unchecked, and no externally recognised certificate results — which may matter if port contracts later demand formal electric-vehicle licences from operators.

Off-the-job training: The haulage training centre course at $800 per driver gives all 9 drivers structured classroom and yard tuition with a recognised electric-vehicle certificate, costing $7,200 in total — small against a $780,000 truck investment. However, drivers are removed from rostered duties during the course, potentially squeezing the 41-minute terminal turnaround, and generic centre content will not match CSL's specific routes, charge-point locations or port procedures without on-site reinforcement.

Decision: CSL should choose on-the-job training for the first wave, adding the haulage centre certificate only for the two most senior drivers who will become in-house trainers. On-the-job delivery is cheapest, route-specific and protects the on-time rate immediately; it also limits disruption while the 12% driver turnover is being fixed. Blanket off-the-job certification for all 9 is rejected as unnecessary spend and roster disruption at launch, though CSL can expand centre training once the fleet beds in and contracts specify formal EV credentials, giving all nine drivers the certificate without paying for a single one during the fragile launch quarter when cash and cover are both tightest.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to CSL.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of the benefits and drawbacks of one or both training methods in the context of CSL.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both training methods in the context of CSL with a well-justified decision covering cost, disruption and route relevance.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how CSL's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $390,000 ÷ ($95 − $69) = $390,000 ÷ $26 = 15,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 15,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $95 − $69 = $26.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $26.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways CSL's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. CSL's managers can compare the 15,000-unit break-even output with actual output of 24,000 units to confirm the shuttle operation is comfortably profitable, with a margin of safety of 9,000 units, informing the pace of the electric truck rollout.
2. Contribution per unit of $26 lets CSL model discounts for high-volume forwarder contracts, for example a cut to $90 would drop contribution to $21, letting managers judge whether zero-emission certificate pricing still covers the $390,000 fixed costs.
3. Knowing fixed costs of $390,000 and contribution per unit helps managers plan monthly instalments on the $480,000 hire purchase, checking the 12 electric trucks will each clear their payments from container moves alone.
4. Managers can use average total cost of $85.25 ($390,000 ÷ 24,000 + $69) to compare diesel versus electric per-unit economics quarter by quarter, quantify the saving from cutting empty running below 14%, and benchmark performance across the $69 variable cost as diesel rises 16.4%.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 15,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $26.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 9,000 units vs 24,000-unit output; forwarder contract discount modelling vs $390,000 fixed costs; hire purchase affordability for the $480,000 agreement and $780,000 investment; and average total cost benchmarking at $85.25 to drive down empty running.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate CSL's financial performance by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for 2024 and 2025. Has CSL's financial performance improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 35.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 40.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 10.0%
Profit Margin 2025 = 15.0%
ROCE 2024 = 15.0%
ROCE 2025 = 20.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 revenue = $2,400,000 and gross profit = $840,000 against cost of sales of $1,560,000; 2025 revenue = $2,880,000 and gross profit = $1,152,000 against cost of sales of $1,728,000. 2024 operating profit = $240,000 against $2,400,000 of revenue (10.0%); 2025 operating profit = $432,000 against $2,880,000 of revenue (15.0%). 2024 capital employed = $1,600,000, 2025 = $2,160,000; interest payable rose from $52,000 to $68,000. 2024 figure: $240,000 ÷ $1,600,000 = 15.0% on capital employed; 2025 figure: $432,000 ÷ $2,160,000 = 20.0%.

Evaluation: CSL's profitability has strengthened decisively. Margins widened because revenue grew $480,000 while cost of sales grew only $168,000, reflecting tighter fuel management, the on-time premium pricing and lower empty running. Operating profit rose by $192,000, easily outpacing the $16,000 rise in interest payable, so the $480,000 hire purchase is well supported. However, capital employed grew 35% from $1,600,000 to $2,160,000 — CSL must keep utilisation high on the electric trucks to stop returns thinning; contracted forwarder rates will need to hold as wages rise 6.3% and diesel-linked surcharges come under scrutiny.

Conclusion: CSL's financial performance has improved. Gross profit margin rose from 35.0% to 40.0%, the operating profit margin rose from 10.0% to 15.0%, and ROCE rose from 15.0% to 20.0%. The gains are broad-based and the electric truck investment is well positioned to extend them, though converting the zero-emission premium into signed forwarder contracts is now the critical step.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both 2024 and 2025 with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate ratio calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost of sales, operating profit and capital employed movements and a justified conclusion on whether CSL's financial performance improved.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for CSL of introducing electric port-shuttle trucks on its container routes.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Electric trucks cut fuel and maintenance costs per port run, helping CSL hold its $95 selling price even as wholesale diesel rose 16.4%, and let it issue the zero-emission delivery certificates that 57% of the 320 surveyed forwarders now require for port contracts. Winning those certified lanes protects the 93.5% on-time rate reputation, lifts the 24,000 units a year toward the 12 trucks' combined capacity, and positions CSL as the default electric shuttle.

Disadvantage: The $780,000 investment plus $480,000 hire purchase commits CSL to fixed instalments regardless of volumes, and the 12 trucks lose productivity to battery charging and turnaround at the depot exactly when the terminal expects 41-minute container moves. Battery technology is also improving quickly, so the new fleet risks partial obsolescence, and 9 drivers still need $800 familiarisation while the 12% labour turnover makes retaining certified electric-truck drivers genuinely hard.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to CSL's research data, costs and expansion.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the 16.4% rise in diesel prices, the 6.3% minimum wage increase and the base interest rate rise to 5.5% will affect CSL. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Diesel price rise (16.4%): Fuel dominates the $69 variable cost of diesel runs. A 16.4% rise on a fuel component of roughly $30 adds about $4.92 per diesel unit — over $118,000 a year across the diesel share of 24,000 units. Margins compress toward $21 contribution unless CSL reprices or surcharges forwarders, but the rise also validates the $780,000 electric truck investment, because each additional electric lane permanently removes diesel exposure from the P&L.

Minimum wage increase (6.3%, to $14.03 per hour): With 64 staff — drivers, yard hands and admin — CSL's wage bill rises by roughly 6.3%. If average hourly pay is around $14.03, one full-time employee costs roughly $29,200 a year, so a 6.3% rise adds about $1,840 per worker — roughly $117,800 across the workforce. That rivals the diesel increase in cash terms and lands as the 12% driver labour turnover peak bites, lifting recruitment and overtime costs alongside the base pay rise.

Interest rate rise (4.75% to 5.5%): The hire purchase instalments are largely fixed, so the 0.75% rise directly affects only new or floating finance CSL might arrange for further trucks or depot charging equipment — perhaps $3,000 to $6,000 a year. It is the least damaging of the three in immediate cash terms and can be managed by fixing finance at negotiation, though it makes further expansion borrowing costlier.

Conclusion: The 16.4% diesel price rise will have the greatest impact. It is the largest single cost exposure in the diesel operation, roughly $118,000 a year at current volumes, it recurs on every future litre, and it cannot be passed through instantly without risking forwarder contracts — while the electric truck rollout both shields CSL and monetises the zero-emission premium. The wage rise is the second most serious threat and demands rostering discipline and profit sharing to retain drivers, while the interest rate move is manageable, though both still require tighter cost control and firmer contract pricing.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to CSL.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on CSL's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three external changes in the context of CSL with a well-justified judgement that the diesel price rise has the greatest impact and why the other two are smaller.
